input.pql: PREDICT COUNT(orders.*, 0, 30, days) > 0 FOR EACH users.user_id

view.name: view_metric_composite_join
view.yaml:
version: 0.1
source: "`{catalog}`.`{schema}`.orders"
joins:
  - name: users
    source: "`{catalog}`.`{schema}`.users"
    on: source.user_id = users.user_id AND users.age > 20
dimensions:
  - name: order_id
    expr: source.order_id
  - name: user_id
    expr: source.user_id
  - name: ts
    expr: source.ts
  - name: price
    expr: source.price
  - name: country
    expr: users.country

why: A join whose on is not one equality of two columns: the reference skips the join and the dimension that reads it (SkippedJoin, DB/metric_view.py:143, :825-909) and says so in one SDMWarning, the view read in part. The view is created in the test schema from the yaml, its sources named with the {catalog} and {schema} placeholders the capture writes (no private name), each part backtick-quoted since Databricks reads a catalog's hyphen only quoted; its joins' on keys are bare, as people write them, so PyYAML reads each as the key true (KO3-40), which the reference reads too (DB/metric_view.py:825-909, join_cfg.get(True))
